page.layout: One printed page of text. Running head at top centre. Verse block in italic, then a rule, then a title with a large initial, then a verse block with a large initial R, ending with a line "D. PHI-" at lower right. No margin notes, no page number, no catchword.

p.i: Et liquidis sub aquis pisces natantes mutitant.
Natura te omnis, denique, ut fidu suorum antistitem.
Hac inter, tibi turbatus, Gesnere, parentat
Beza tuus, Vati Gates, et amicus amico;

main_text.head: D. MARTINI LVTHERI magni, diuinitus ad Ecclesiæ Christianæ, aduersus Antichristum Romanum instaurandæ, assertionem missi, Memoriæ.
main_text.p: ROma orbem domuit, Roma sibi Papa subegit Viribus illa suis, fraudibus iste suis,

p.i: Quanto isto maior Lutherus, maior et illa,
Illu illamque Syno qui domuit calamo?
I nunc, Alcidem memorato Gracia mendax,
Lutheri ad calamum ferrea clava nihil

page.notes: Large initial R of "Roma" is a woodcut-style letter, read as R. Several words in the first verse block and the Greek/Hebrew-like forms ("Syno", "Gracia") are doubtful; the line "Reb eantia" appears to be "Rebeantia" as printed. Lower page contains scattered specks and show-through, not transcribed.
